subject_name: Law of Banking and Negotiable Instruments
summary: The examination pattern for Law of Banking and Negotiable Instruments heavily balances foundational legal concepts with practical problem-solving. Questions frequently test core statutory definitions and relationships between bankers and customers across Part A (short notes) and Part B (essay questions), alongside specific case-law or hypothetical scenarios in Part C. Topics regarding negotiable instruments, checks, and statutory protections for banks emerge as dominant fixtures across multiple years. Overall, the syllabus is well-covered, with structural emphasis on the Banking Regulation Act and the Negotiable Instruments Act.
